clinician.trajectory_summary: A Japanese infant boy born at 36 weeks with hepatosplenomegaly, microcephaly, and ocular abnormalities was suspected of congenital CMV infection. Maternal CMV seropositivity was confirmed. Ophthalmoscopic exam on admission showed posterior vessel dilation, demarcation lines at the temporal peripheral zone, and arteriovenous anastomosis without chorioretinitis. Fluorescein angiography on day 4 revealed filling delay, an arterio-venous anastomosis, and avascular peripheral retina without leakage. CMV-DNA was detected in the aqueous humor, confirming ocular infection. Antiviral therapy with oral valgancyclovir led to regression of vessel abnormalities and improvement of anastomosis after 6 days of treatment, confirming clinical response. Despite lacking infant urine and blood CMV-DNA PCR results, the diagnosis of ocular CMV infection was accurately established by clinical, imaging, virological eye fluid evidence, and treatment response.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Ophthalmoscopic examination revealed posterior vessel dilation, a demarcation line at the temporal peripheral zone in both eyes, and an arteriovenous anastomosis in the right eye without chorioretinitis.
Fluorescein angiography on day 4 showed filling delay, arterio-venous anastomosis, and a small avascular zone at the peripheral retina without leakage.
CMV-DNA positive in aqueous humor confirmed viral presence in ocular fluids.
After 6 days of oral valgancyclovir therapy, vessel dilation regressed completely and arterio-venous anastomosis improved markedly.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: absence of chorioretinitis and confirmation of CMV-DNA in ocular fluid support CMV etiology

remaining_uncertainties: No documented CMV-DNA PCR results in infant urine or whole blood were provided to confirm systemic viral load
Long-term ophthalmological follow-up and neurodevelopment outcome data are not reported
